decisive_items: a left periprosthetic soft‐tissue mass measuring 9 × 8 × 10 cm, without bony involvement or bone‐marrow edema
Serum cobalt and chromium levels were within normal limits
response.rationale: Large periprosthetic soft-tissue mass with normal metal ion levels and negative cultures favors adverse local tissue reaction (ALTR) over metallosis, infection, or osteolysis; clinical progression and mass exclude bursitis/tendinosis.

rejected.why: Negative cultures and only mildly elevated inflammatory markers make chronic infection unlikely.
Tendinosis cannot explain a 9×8×10 cm periprosthetic mass.
Normal serum cobalt and chromium levels argue against metallosis.
Negative cultures and lack of systemic signs do not support infection.
Unchanged radiographs and no bony involvement contradict osteolysis.
Initial bursitis diagnosis was contradicted by progression and new neurologic symptoms with a large mass.
